title: Format Robustness Prompt Corpus v1
summary: Working corpus of prompt templates and target schemas intended to stress formatting, quoting, typing and structural adherence when onboarding generation models. Emphasis on real-world oddities: missing keys, extra keys, unicode, escaped characters, and schema combinators (oneOf/allOf).
purpose: Create a repeatable prompt+schema suite to exercise model output formatting robustness and to catch regressions where models start returning invalid JSON or subtly malformed structures after model or inference stack changes.
test_plan: Run the full corpus against each candidate model version and quantify: JSON validity rate, schema-validation pass rate, field-level type-accuracy, and common formatting failures (single quotes, trailing commas, commentary text). Store raw outputs, validation errors, and diff to golden examples. Rerun daily on CI for dedicated onboarding experiments and weekly for production regression scans.
prompt_set: Strict JSON only. Given the schema (DELIMITED BY ###SCHEMA###) and the user prompt (DELIMITED BY ###PROMPT###), produce only the JSON object that validates against the schema. Do not include any explanation, backticks, or extra text. Example inputs may include unicode, line breaks and long strings.

Schema-first: Here is the JSON Schema: ###SCHEMA###. Now convert the following natural-language invoice description into a JSON document that matches the schema exactly: ###PROMPT###. Only output valid JSON; formatting (spacing/newlines) doesn't matter but must be syntactically correct.

Edge-case enforcement: Produce a JSON object that matches the schema but intentionally tests these edge cases when applicable: empty arrays, null where allowed, numeric strings when integers are required (should fail), and very large integers. Output JSON only.

Robust-key-order: Given a schema with required fields [customerId, items, total], output JSON where the keys are deliberately shuffled (not necessarily original order) and still valid. The evaluator should not assume ordering.

Extra-properties stress: For schemas that set additionalProperties:false, ensure no extra keys appear. For schemas that allow additionalProperties:true, include 1–2 extra random fields with short values. Output JSON only.
Quoting and escaping: Convert the text input into a JSON string field that includes newlines, quotes, backslashes, and non-ascii characters. Ensure correct escaping so the overall JSON is valid.
Minimal output: When a lot of optional fields exist, emit only the required fields and valid empty structures (e.g., empty arrays) unless the prompt asks to populate optionals. Output JSON only.

OneOf/Alt schema: When the schema uses oneOf for a field (e.g., id can be integer or string), choose the simplest valid variant but keep track of which branch was used in the metadata logged by the evaluator. Output JSON only.
Array boundary: For array fields with minItems or maxItems, produce outputs that test min, max, and just-over-max (to check validator catches violation). Output JSON only.
No commentary: For each test, the model must not include any commentary, markdown fences, or natural language. Any non-JSON output is considered a hard fail.
test_cases: Natural language invoice: 'Invoice 2025-001 for Acme Corp (ID 42). Items: 2x SKU:ABC123 qty 2, 1x SKU:Ω-µ-∆ qty 1. Total: 329.50. Customer email: billing+europe@acme.co.uk'
Identifier variant: 'Create an object for type=user with id US-000123 and tags ["beta", "imported"]'
Deep pattern: 'Make a root.payload with keys x_region, x_zone each having value and count fields. region value may be null.'
Escaping case: 'User provided text: She said "I\'ll be there\nby 10:00 — use backslash \\ and emoji 😊'
Array limits: 'Create items array with 0 items (should fail minItems), then with 1 item, then with 51 items when maxItems=50 to test violation handling.'
grading_rules: Primary check: output must be parseable JSON (json.loads). Any parse error -> hard fail.
Schema validation: Use Ajv/everit/jsonschema to validate against provided schema. If additionalProperties=false and extra keys exist -> fail.
Type checks: numeric fields must be numbers (not numeric strings) unless schema explicitly allows string. If type mismatch -> record field-level failure.
Quoting rules: Strings must use double quotes; single quotes are invalid JSON. If single quotes appear at top level -> fail.
No extra text: Any non-JSON prefix/suffix must mark a hard fail. Logs should capture first 200 characters of offending output for triage.
OneOf tracking: If schema uses oneOf/multiple branches, evaluator must log which branch matched. If none matched -> fail.
Edge-case logging: Record occurrences of trailing commas, comments (// or /* */), and unescaped control characters.
Partial success: If JSON parses but fails schema, capture validator errors and classify into categories (missing required, type-mismatch, additional-property, pattern-failure).
expected_behavior: High-quality model: >95% JSON-parseable outputs and >90% schema-pass on required fields for small schemas (<=10 keys).
Regression detection: New model versions should not increase rate of single-quote outputs or trailing commas beyond a small baseline. Any +5% regression triggers review.
Tolerance: For schemas allowing additionalProperties:true, model may include extra metadata fields but values should follow simple types (string/number/null).
known_issues: Models sometimes wrap JSON in markdown fences (```json). We treat this as non-JSON and fail the test unless the output inside fences is extracted by post-processing (post-processing allowed in CI but counted as weaker signal).
Tendency to prefer strings for numeric identifiers (e.g., "42" vs 42). OneOf schemas can mask this; flag occurrences where schema expected integer but string provided.
Unicode and emoji frequently cause incorrect escaping (e.g., unescaped surrogate pairs) on some runtime bindings. Log full raw output when unicode appears.
When prompts ask for extra-properties, some models invent very long nested objects; enforce a max nesting depth in the evaluator to protect downstream parsers.
run_instructions: CI job: for each model candidate, iterate prompt_set x schemas x test_cases. Capture raw output, try strict JSON parse; if parse succeeds, validate. Save payloads and validator results under artifact path, produce summary CSV: total, parsed, schema_pass, key_failures. Feedback loop: attach failing prompts to GitHub issue with examples.
notes_to_reviewers: This is a working corpus — we will expand with real customer snippets and more pathological cases (malformed CSV in fields, HTML fragments, SQL injections) after initial runs. Please prioritize tests that catch additionalProperties errors and quoting mistakes.
